newsitem.title: USA: Senate panel ups US defense orders for Conn. firms.
newsitem.headline: Senate panel ups US defense orders for Conn. firms.

text.p: Defense funds approved by the U.S. Senate Armed Services Committee include billions of dollars for Connecticut companies, officials said on Friday.

The fiscal year 1998 defense authorization bill, marked up in the Senate committee, will particularly help United Technologies Corp and General Dynamics Corp unit Electric Boat Corp., Conn. U.S. Sen. Joe Lieberman (D) said.
United Technologies is based in Hartford, and submarine-maker Electric Boat is in Groton, Conn.
The legislation calls for some $250.7 million for completion of the third and final Seawolf submarine at Electric Boat -- an increase of $17 million over President Bill Clinton's request.
It also calls for $2.6 billion for the New Attack Submarine, to be built in a historic teaming by Electric Boat and rival Newport News Shipbuilding.

There is also $2.46 billion for the C-17 airlifter, for which United Technologies unit Pratt & Whitney provides the engines -- an increase of nearly $160 million over the amount in the FY 1997 authorization, Lieberman said.
Some 18 more Black Hawk helicopters worth $127 million, built by United Technologies unit Sikorsky Aircraft, have been added.
"Overall I was very pleased with what we approved for Connecticut projects, because we're operating in a context that overall defense numbers are dropping," Lieberman said.
U.S. Rep. Jim Maloney (D-Conn.) called the authorization "a huge victory for our state's economy."
He said the additional Black Hawk helicopters would result in the saving of some 1,000 jobs at Sikorsky.
